names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 17 iunie, «Sfinții Mucenici Manuil, Savel și Ismail».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 17 Ιουνίου, «Άγιοι Μανουήλ, Σαβέλ και Ισμαήλ», and its page head «Άγιος Σαβέλ (; - 362)», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 17. јун ст. ст., „Свети мученици Мануил, Савел и Исмаил“, where it is the second of the three names — „Свети мученици“ stands at the head of the three and comes off, and the heading gives him no epithet and no country, so the bare forename is what the source gives; the «of Persia» of the display name is the corpus’s own disambiguation and not anything this heading prints. `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM for «Савел», so there is no fold — and the same was measured for his two brothers’ forms on the same run, all three clear.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 17 iunie — «Sfinții Mucenici Manuil, Savel și Ismail»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 17ης Ιουνίου — «Άγιοι Μανουήλ, Σαβέλ και Ισμαήλ»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 17 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. It is plainly the same martyr: one of the three brothers out of Persia beheaded under Julian, whom the folder's Romanian row already keeps on 17 June, and saint.gr's page head gives the year 362. The page also prints an apolytikion of nine which names these three together with the six of Apollonia whom the same day keeps; that shared text is recorded on the Apollonia folders and not here. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 30.06.2026 (17. јун ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Мануил, Савел и Исмаил“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry, second of the three names it enumerates. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 17 June is the same menologion number this folder’s Romanian and Greek rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. THE COMPANY, COUNTED BY §5. „Свети мученици Мануил, Савел и Исмаил“ enumerates **three** names, therefore up to three folders — and all three exist, one per brother, written on 24 September off doxologia’s single line and filled out on 1 October off saint.gr. So the entry costs no new folder and takes three rows, each the same heading quoted whole, which is how a company of this corpus is cited. A THIRD BOOK ON A STORY TWO BOOKS ALREADY TOLD DIFFERENTLY, AND IT SETTLES ONE THING. doxologia had them numbered in the army and serving Alamundar king of Persia, and had the refusal begin at a sacrificial feast; saint.gr had them come to Constantinople on an embassy and happen to see the emperor sacrificing **at Chalcedon**. This book has both halves and puts them together: they were „високи чиновници код цара Аламундара“, high officials at the court of king Alamundar, sent to the Apostate „да воде преговоре и утврде мир између царством Персијским и Грчко-римским“, to negotiate and establish peace between the Persian and the Greco-Roman empires — and the feast of the idols was „у Халкидону“, at Chalcedon, which is where saint.gr put it and where doxologia did not. **Two of the three books now agree on Chalcedon and the third is silent rather than contrary**, so the life says so and no date, place field or office is written off it. **`soldier` IS LEFT ALONE AND NOT ENDORSED.** The folders hold `martyr` and `soldier`; `soldier` came off doxologia’s „numbered in the army“, and this book says instead that they were high civil officials. `types_add` is not used, nothing is removed — there is no removal key and a disagreement between two books is not a defect — and the new paragraph states what this book says. WHAT IS NEW IN THE MARTYRDOM. They declared themselves foreign subjects, come as envoys of the Persian king for the establishing of peace and for nothing else, and said that they held it unworthy to bow to dead idols and offer them sacrifice; thrown into prison, brought out the next day and disputed with about the faith, they were „неодољива и непоколебљива“, irresistible and unshakeable. **They were tied naked to trees, beaten, and scraped with iron brushes** — a torture neither of the other books has — and through the whole of it they prayed to God with thanksgiving for the torments, in the book’s own quotation marks: „О слатки Исусе, ове су нам муке слатке због љубави Твоје!“ **An angel of God appeared to them, comforted them and took away all their pain**, which is also new. THE EARTH OPENING, AND THE HALF OF IT THE CORPUS DID NOT HAVE. doxologia had the ground open and receive the bodies so that the fire could not touch them. This book has that **and the other half**: „тела мученика потом земља изврже, да би их хришћани нашли и чесно сахранили“ — afterwards the earth cast the bodies back out, so that the Christians might find them and bury them honourably. The sentence „насупрот свима међународним односима“, against all international usage, is this book’s own and is written in. NO YEAR, AND THE ONE THE CORPUS ALREADY CITES IS NOT MINE. `dates` is **null** on all three folders and stays null: this book states no year for the embassy, the feast, the torture or the beheading. **The only year any of these folders has ever cited is saint.gr’s page head «(; - 362)», quoted inside `manuel-of-persia`’s `el` name note and recorded in no `dates` object** — a year cited and never recorded, which is `date-citation-audit`’s own class of finding and the author’s to decide, not a reader’s to write off a book that does not say it. **No year is derived from the Apostate** either: his reign, his Persian campaign and his death are all in this entry, an emperor is not a source for a year, and a year reached by arithmetic off a reign is refused twice over. NO NEW ROWS, AND THE APOSTATE IS WRITTEN WITHOUT HIS NAME. The two brothers are already in each folder’s `related` and already linked in its prose, so nothing is added. **`цар Јулијан Одступник` is written as «the Apostate» and not by his forename**: no folder holds the emperor, `ls saints | grep -i julian` returns thirty-two folders that are other men and women of the name, an emperor in a life is not a relation, and `related-floor` reads a prose name as well as a linked one — the folders’ older prose from the other two books does name him, and that prose is left exactly as it stands. King Alamundar is named, as he already is in the older prose, and `ls saints | grep -iE 'mundar|mundhir'` holds nobody. No rows for the Persian king’s army, the informers, the servants who fled or the magnates at the sacrifice. No `locations`: Chalcedon is one clause. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE DAY’S OTHER ENTRY IS REFUSED, AND **ON IDENTITY RATHER THAN ON ABSENCE**, WHICH IS NEW IN THIS WAVE. „Преподобни Пиор, отшелник нитријски“ — Pior, hermit of Nitria, who never once sat down to a table to eat but ate standing and working, saying „Нећу да се занимам једењем као послом него као узгредицом“; who came to a council called to judge a brother’s sin carrying a sack of sand on his back and a little purse of sand on his breast, and said that the sack was his own sins, which he does not see, and the purse his brother’s, which he is to judge, at which the whole brotherhood was ashamed and cried out „То је пут спасења!“; who lived a hundred years and reposed in the Lord in the fourth century. **`pior-the-recluse` exists and did not get this row.** `ls saints | grep -iE 'pior|nitria'` returns `pior-the-recluse`, `john-of-nitria`, `or-of-nitria`, `pamvo-of-nitria` and `ten-thousand-of-nitria`; the name is held by exactly one folder and nothing else in the corpus reads like it. But that folder has one book and one sentence, and the sentence is that saint.gr **has no details of the life of this Russian saint**, kept on **4 October**, as «Όσιος Πίωρ ο Έγκλειστος». So the two share a rare name and the rank of venerable, and they share nothing else: one day against another, a recluse against a hermit of Nitria, and a Russian against the Egyptian desert, with no life on the Greek side to read the person off. **Match on the day and the person, never on the name alone** — so this is an open identity question and not an upgrade, no row was written, and the hundred years and the fourth century this book gives were not written anywhere either. It is the author’s to decide whether `pior-the-recluse` is this man.

hymns.text: Mucenicii Tăi, Doamne, întru nevoinţele lor, cununile nesctricăciunii au dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru. Că având tăria Ta, pe chinuitori au învins; zdrobit-au şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lor, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfinților Mucenici Manuil, Savel și Ismail. It is the common troparion of martyrs, printed for the whole company and naming none of them; the reading «nesctricăciunii» is the page's own spelling.

english.text: Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their contest received from Thee, our God, the crowns of incorruption; for having Thy strength, they overthrew the tormentors and broke also the feeble insolence of the demons. At their prayers, O Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Οἱ τῆς εὐσεβείας ὑπέρμαχοι, καὶ τῆς ἀσεβείας ἀντίπαλοι, Μανουὴλ θεόπνευστε, καὶ Ἰσμαὴλ θαυμάσιε, καὶ Σαβὲλ ἀξιάγαστε, παῥῥησίᾳ τὸν Χριστὸν, Υἱὸν Θεοῦ κηρύξαντες, τὸ αἷμα ὑμῶν ὑπὲρ Αὐτοῦ ἐξεχέατε· ὃν δυσωποῦντες μὴ παύσητε, τοῦ σωθῆναι τὰς ψυχάς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, ᾌχος δ´ — the third of three apolytikia on the page of «Άγιοι Μανουήλ, Σαβέλ και Ισμαήλ», and the one that names all three

english.text: O champions of piety and adversaries of impiety, God-inspired Manuel, wondrous Ismael and admirable Sabel, having proclaimed Christ boldly as the Son of God, you poured out your blood for him; cease not to entreat him, that our souls may be saved.

hymns.text: Οἱ τρεῖς θεῖοι Μάρτυρες οἱ ἐκ Περσίδος, τὸν Σταυρὸν ἀράμενοι, οὐκ ἐδειλίασαν ποινὰς, ἀλλ’ ἐν σταδίῳ ἐκήρυξαν, τὸν ἐν Μονάδι Θεὸν Τρισυπόστατον.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, ᾌχος δ´, Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον — the second of two kontakia on the page of «Άγιοι Μανουήλ, Σαβέλ και Ισμαήλ», naming the three out of Persia

english.text: The three divine martyrs out of Persia took up the Cross and did not flinch at the punishments, but in the arena proclaimed God, one in unity and three in person.
